findings.description: Statistics added without citation: Meta's 3.98 billion monthly active people (Q4 2025) and Google's estimated 8.5 billion daily searches appear as parenthetical data without source URLs or in-text citations. The site's fair witness standard requires sourced data points, especially specific figures with temporal qualifiers.
findings.suggestion: Add citation links for both figures. Meta's Q4 2025 earnings report and a reliable source for Google's search volume (Statista, SparkToro, or similar) would anchor these claims. Format: parenthetical inline links or footnotes consistent with the post's existing citation style (Author, Year).
findings.context: Recommendation algorithms at companies like Meta and Google concentrate decision-making power over billions of users' information environments (Meta reported 3.98 billion monthly active people across its family of apps in Q4 2025; Google processes an estimated 8.5 billion searches per day).

findings.description: Date precision reduced from 'March 17, 1977' to 'in 1977' during URL correction. The link fix corrected a wrong URL (previously pointed to the Senate transmittal document instead of the UN General Assembly speech), but the edit also dropped the specific date. Fair witness discipline favors maximum available precision.
findings.suggestion: Restore the specific date: 'His [address to the United Nations](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-the-united-nations-general-assembly-0) on March 17, 1977 reinforced...' The American Presidency Project page confirms the date.
findings.context: Carter's human rights-centered foreign policy made treaty signature a priority. His [address to the United Nations](https://www.presidency.ucsb.edu/documents/address-the-united-nations-general-assembly-0) in 1977 reinforced the administration's commitment to human rights treaty ratification.

epistemic_flags: Google search volume figure (8.5B/day) lacks a single authoritative source — multiple third-party estimates circulate with varying figures. The finding flags the absence of citation, not the accuracy of the number itself.
